misconceptions.description: Assuming a facial-recognition tool that is accurate on average is therefore fair to every student group
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites an overall accuracy number and concludes the tool is equitable
misconceptions.feedback: Average accuracy hides subgroup error. Check the breakdown by skin tone or group; a gap that falls on one group is an equity tension, not a rounding error.

misconceptions.description: Producing a yes-or-no verdict on facial recognition instead of mapping the competing values and a negotiated decision
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes 'it is biased, ban it' or 'it saves time, use it' with one pole only
misconceptions.feedback: A tension map names both poles with evidence and records a negotiated decision. Replace the verdict with the conflict and the conditions under which the decision could change.

misconceptions.description: Framing the case only as instructional time versus equity and missing the data-retention privacy tension
misconceptions.trigger: learner maps only two poles and never asks where face templates are stored or for how long
misconceptions.feedback: Surface the hidden privacy pole. Ask where biometric templates are kept, by whom, and for how long, then add it to the tension map.
